scope_3_categories.category_name: Fuel- and energy-related activities (not included in Scope 1 or Scope 2)

emissions_targets.sbti_target_description: Net-Zero targets validated by SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard in August 2022. Scope 1 and 2 target aligned with 1.5°C (76% absolute reduction by 2030 vs. 2021, equivalent to 90% vs. 2017). Scope 3 target aligned with well-below 2°C (25% absolute reduction by 2030 vs. 2021). Long-term net-zero target of 90% absolute reduction across all scopes by 2050 vs. 2021.

key_levers: Energy sufficiency and efficiency actions at sites (reduce energy consumption)
Electrification of sites and vehicle fleet (switch from fossil fuels to electricity)
Renewable electricity sourcing (bundled/unbundled certificates and on-site generation)
SF6 phase-down in products and reduction of SF6 leaks at sites (AirSeT SF6-free circuit breakers)
Supplier engagement via The Zero Carbon Project (top 1,000 suppliers target 50% Scope 1+2 reduction by 2025) and eco-design of products to reduce upstream and downstream Scope 3 emissions

breakdown.note: EUR 39.8M and EUR 14.4M are itemised 2024 CapEx; total transition plan CapEx of EUR 41.6M reported separately as aligned to decarbonization levers tracking Scope 1 and 2 only

internal_carbon_price.scope_of_application: Two mechanisms: (1) Carbon prices used in climate risk assessment applied to full GHG footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3; 55,792,899 tCO2eq covered), with prices ranging from 0 to 647 EUR/tCO2eq depending on country and scenario. (2) Marginal Abatement Cost Curve (MACC) analysis applied to carbon-intensive raw materials in upstream Scope 3 (~2,540,000 tCO2eq; ~4% of total Scope 3, ~25% of upstream categories), with no fixed carbon price but varying marginal costs.

methodology.calculation_standard: GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard and GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard; compliant with ISO 14069 principles; all GHGs included in the Kyoto Protocol expressed in tCO2eq; Scope 2 calculated under both market-based and location-based approaches per GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance
methodology.assurance_level: Reasonable assurance on Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions; limited assurance on Scope 3 GHG emissions and SSI/SSE indicators

data_quality_flags.flag: Inconsistency between total Scope 1+2 (market-based) figures across sections. Page 150 CSRD table reports Scope 1 = 106,360 tCO2eq and Scope 2 market-based = 37,348 tCO2eq, summing to 143,708 tCO2eq. Page 348 GRI table confirms this sum as 'Total Scopes 1 and 2 GHG emissions (market-based) = 143,708 tCO2eq'. However, page 502 compensation section states '2024 emissions amounted to 144,309 tons of CO2' for Scope 1 and 2, a difference of 601 tCO2eq vs. the audited figure. No reconciliation is provided.

Scope 3 upstream emissions showed a year-on-year increase of approximately 3.2% (from 7,766,994 tCO2eq in 2023 to 8,017,665 tCO2eq in 2024 per page 349), while the narrative on page 141 states 'upstream emissions have decreased by 2.7% since 2021'. The Board compensation review on page 502 attributes the 2024 increase to volume growth and expanded CSRD reporting scope capturing entities previously estimated. This methodology change creates a restatement risk but no formal restatement of the 2030 target baseline is disclosed.

Capital goods (Scope 3 Category 2) and fuel- and energy-related activities (Category 3) showed very large year-on-year increases in 2024 vs. 2023: Category 2 increased from 55,361 to 161,033 tCO2eq (+191%) and Category 3 increased from 40,652 to 100,126 tCO2eq (+146%). Footnote on page 349 attributes this to a methodology change in 2024, but no quantified restatement of prior years or explanation of the specific change is provided, limiting comparability.

The report states on page 112 that 'Schneider Electric's total carbon emissions (56 million tons in 2024) are mostly originating from Scope 3' and references a 'Net-Zero emissions by 2025' target, which appears to be a drafting error. The Company's public commitment is Net-Zero ready operations by 2030 and full value chain Net-Zero by 2050, not 2025. The 2025 milestone is 'carbon neutral operations', a different concept involving carbon credits.

Business travel (Scope 3 Category 6) increased sharply from 60,702 tCO2eq in 2023 to 161,046 tCO2eq in 2024, a 165% increase. Footnote 7 on page 349 notes that starting in 2024, radiative forcing of air freight and air travel was included. This represents a significant methodology change affecting year-on-year comparability for this category, but no restated 2023 figure is provided.

The percentage of Scope 3 GHG calculated using primary data is disclosed as only 1.37% (page 150), predominantly from paid freight and some aluminum procurement. This is a very low primary data coverage for a footprint of ~55.6 MtCO2eq. The large majority of Scope 3 (including Category 1 purchased goods at 6.6 MtCO2eq and Category 11 use of sold products at 42.6 MtCO2eq) relies on spend-based or LCA-based estimation methods, creating significant estimation uncertainty.

The LTIP 2024 carbon targets were revised mid-cycle in February 2025 (page 502) because (i) the Scope 1+2 target was already over-achieved after one year and (ii) the Scope 3 upstream intensity target was deemed unreachable, partly due to expanded CSRD reporting scope. This raises a question about the robustness of the original target-setting and the degree to which CSRD scope changes were anticipated when setting executive compensation metrics.

Use of sold products (Scope 3 Category 11) represents 42,598,039 tCO2eq or approximately 76.5% of total Scope 3. These emissions are calculated based on products sold in the reporting year and cumulated over their full expected lifetime (up to 30 years), using forward-looking IEA Stated Policies Scenario grid intensity. This lifetime-based accounting methodology, while compliant with GHG Protocol, means the reported figure is not the actual GHG emitted in 2024, but a forward-looking stock concept. This is disclosed but may not be immediately apparent to users comparing the figure to peers using a different convention.
